ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: in the figure, the Sun is located in the middle-lower part, and one Earth position is drawn at the lower left and another at the upper right, labeled P and Q respectively. The Earth's axial tilt direction is drawn for both Earth positions, and dashed lines and solid lines indicate sunlight illumination and related reference lines; the letters L and S are marked at small-angle positions in the Sun-Earth illumination relationship and belong to the same type of inclination angle. Reasoning: the question states that when Earth is located at point P its revolution speed is relatively slow, indicating that near P it is close to aphelion, and the time is around the summer solstice in the Northern Hemisphere. Around the two solstices, the direct solar point reaches the tropics, and the solar declination reaches its maximum value; this maximum value is equal to the obliquity of the ecliptic, and is also manifested as the maximum angle that can be formed between Earth's axis and the terminator line. Therefore, the degrees of the letters L and S in the figure are equal to the maximum angle between Earth's axis and the terminator line.
